target_customer: Quantitative researchers and data scientists working in R and RStudio
problem: Quant and data workflows in R lack an integrated AI coding assistant.
business_model: Subscription for an AI enabled IDE (launch pricing $20 per month for 500 queries)
product_category: AI coding assistant for data science and quantitative trading

founders.name: Jorge Guerra
education: Harvard '24, was a PhD student in biophysics

founders.name: William Nickols
education: Harvard '24, was a PhD student in biostatistics

technical_complexity.rationale: Early product Rao is a fork of RStudio with an embedded AI assistant, relying on third party models.

defensibility.rationale: Thin wrapper over existing models and an open source IDE; copyable quickly.

market_need_then: Cursor style assistants did not serve R users well per the founders' Show HN framing; no spend data found.

identity.logo: Logo image on a sparse founders page, not described

brand_strength.rationale: No brand evidence found; name is easily confused with Lotus and Lota brands in search.

pivots.from: AI coding assistant in RStudio (Rao, Show HN 2025-07)
pivots.to: AI for quantitative trading (YC one liner)

outcome_analysis: Lotas launched an RStudio based AI assistant on Hacker News in July 2025 and describes itself as AI for quantitative trading. The site is sparse and no funding, customers or outcome are public, so the story is too early to read; the product's thin moat is the main visible risk.
notes: Funding search found nothing for Lotas (results were other companies). Competitor search returned mostly 2026 AI trading startups, none dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Show HN content seen only through a reposting blog. The prior employers of founders are not listed.
